subject: SEV1: Tokenization regression — customer-facing ETA & remediation pact
messages:
From: QuantifAI <ops@quantifai.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Tokenization outputs shifted in production (urgent)

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a spike in tokenization mismatch errors across our ingestion stream at ~08:58 PDT. Downstream model scoring is failing for ~12% of requests with a 500-level error (tokenization exception). This is blocking critical batch jobs and real-time traffic.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on the inference runtime or tokenizer models? We are pausing new deployments but need an ETA.

Attached: sample_error.log (snip)

—Jared
QuantifAI SRE
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: QuantifAI <ops@quantifai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tokenization outputs shifted in production (urgent)

Jared — thanks for the alert and the sample. We’ve triaged this and opened an incident bridge.

Short answers up front:
- We are investigating a tokenization regression that looks correlated with a runtime packaging change deployed at ~02:00 UTC.
- We will open a private bridge in the next 10 minutes and share an ETA within 30 minutes.

Immediate next steps:
1) I’m bringing Ben (runtime lead) and Laura (CS lead) into the bridge to coordinate fixes and customer comms.
2) Please share the complete error sample and indicate whether you can switch traffic to the passive fallback model (instructions in the doc I linked below).

We’ll update in the bridge; if you prefer phone, share a dial.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, QuantifAI <ops@quantifai.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:29:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tokenization outputs shifted in production (urgent)

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 09:11 Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jared — thanks for the alert and the sample. We’ve triaged this and opened an incident bridge.

Quick technical summary from runtime: after initial scans we see a packaging/charset edge in the tokenizer shim where certain multibyte sequences are being re-encoded when a specific kernel path is used. Root cause likely a regression introduced in the 2027-04-12 runtime packaging (build 20270412.02).

Mitigation options available now:
- Short-term: revert to build 20270410.* on affected fleet (can be done in 12–18 minutes but requires rolling restarts of the node pool).
- Workaround: enable the legacy tokenizer shim (no restart required, toggle via runtime flag). Performance impact estimated <2% p99.

We recommend: enable legacy shim for affected customers immediately, then schedule a controlled rolling revert for the dedicated pools tomorrow if needed.

I’ve started the toggle in staging and will push to the affected region after QuantifAI confirms.

Attachments: mitigation-checklist.pdf (initial checklist)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: QuantifAI <ops@quantifai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:02:19 -07:00
Subject: SEV1 update — immediate mitigation & customer-facing ETA (10:02 PDT)

Hi Jared & team,

Thank you for the quick report and the error samples. We now have a clear mitigation path and a concrete ETA for QuantifAI:

Summary (what we know):
- Impact: tokenization exceptions affecting ~12% of requests in us-west-2.
- Probable cause: regression in runtime packaging (build 20270412.02) that alters byte handling in the tokenizer shim.

Mitigation (what we’re doing now):
- Enabling the legacy tokenizer shim for QuantifAI (no restart) — currently rolling; expected completion by 10:10 PDT.
- If the toggle does not fully remediate, we will perform a controlled revert of the affected build (estimated 12–18 minutes, requires rolling node restarts).

ETA & commitments:
- ETA for initial remediation (toggle in place): 10:10 PDT (8 minutes from now).
- ETA for full validation and monitoring: 11:00 PDT.
- We will host a short 15-minute executive update at 11:15 PDT to review impact, mitigation, and compensatory steps.

Customer ask: please confirm whether you can enable traffic to the passive fallback model while we validate. If you cannot, we will prioritize the revert.

We are prioritizing this as SEV1. I am assigning Laura to own customer comms and credits, Ben to own remediation, and David to run the postmortem timeline.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident bridge: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/INC-5923
- Live timeline (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c/quantifai-incident-notes
- Initial mitigation checklist: mitigation-checklist.pdf

I’ll post again when the toggle completes.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: QuantifAI <ops@quantifai.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

> - Impact: tokenization exceptions affecting ~12% of requests in us-west-2.

Thanks for the rapid response and the clear timeline. Toggle to legacy shim completed at ~10:09 PDT and we observed error rate drop to <0.5% by 10:15 PDT. We validated the passive fallback model switch and will keep traffic there while you finish validation.

Appreciate the offer of credits; we’ll coordinate with Laura on HR and billing. Please share the postmortem timeline and the remediation plan for preventing recurrence.

Attachments: downtime-screenshot.png, incident-timeline.csv

—Jared
